subject: general
question:
In the given figure, angle ABC = 65 degrees and angle ACD = 120 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle BAC?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ffc013ed64f4efb99ef508a2a8aca9e3eacc7125967ec0fbead4e988c73741fd.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Exterior Angle Theorem: The exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC

120° = ∠BAC + 65°

∠BAC = 120° − 65° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠ABC = 65°, ∠ACD = 120°

**Formula Used:** Linear pair property and angle sum property of a triangle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ddcdbf86e2eaecc6dbbd4e6ada3ebc4f19aecaad947ceb1a13e8c95b3dc278f4.png] 

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ACD = 180° (Linear pair on line BD)

⇒ ∠ACB + 120° = 180°

⇒ ∠ACB = 180° − 120° = 60°

⇒ In ▵ABC: ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ ∠BAC + 65° + 60° = 180°

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 125° = 55°

**∴ The correct answer is 55°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two remote interior angles.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles in any triangle is always 180°.

Linear Pair of Angles

Angles on a straight line that are adjacent to each other always add up to 180°.
